# Remaining real-user requirements — 13 October 2026

**Arcane has a usable unsigned 0.1 development preview and substantial verified components. A fully usable Roblox development application, creator beta and full commercial product are not proven.** This audit preserves the complete original product scope. A smaller milestone, successful fixture, static template or provider handoff does not retire a requirement.

Audit inputs: [PRODUCT_PLAN](../PRODUCT_PLAN.md), [TECHNICAL_SPEC](../TECHNICAL_SPEC.md), [PROVIDER_NATIVE_FEATURES](../PROVIDER_NATIVE_FEATURES.md), [CUSTOM_SKILLS](../CUSTOM_SKILLS.md), all **222** rows of [FEATURE_CATALOG](../FEATURE_CATALOG.csv), [BUILD_ROADMAP](../BUILD_ROADMAP.md), [current ledger](tasks.json), [README](../../README.md), actual implementation and retained proofs. The catalogue's `planned` labels and ledger's `verified_component` labels are not the verdicts below. Older prose claiming no Electron/inference/custom composition is superseded by the narrowly scoped evidence inspected here.

Changes owned by this sidecar: this document and `runtime/verification/requirements-audit-20261013.json` only. No production source, tests, scripts, skills, original plans or ledger was changed. No build/regression, provider turn, API purchase, Studio operation or installation was run. The parent's frozen full regression is independent and is not claimed green by this audit.

## Verdict rules

| State | Meaning |
|---|---|
| proven | The stated invariant has direct inspected implementation/artifact evidence at the specified scope. It does not certify adjacent features. |
| contradicted | An inspected file/artifact positively conflicts with the original requirement or an asserted completion. Contract drift is identified separately from an unauthorized change. |
| incomplete | A meaningful implementation/proof exists, but part of the requirement or its necessary real-user acceptance is open. |
| missing | No implementation/acceptance artifact for that requirement was found in the inspected production surface. Definitions, recipes and prospective handoffs are not execution. |

Saved reports are authoritative for their recorded run, not for the evolving checkout. Source/test definitions establish executable boundaries, not that their tests ran or that native acceptance passed. This audit's JSON pins inspected file hashes and records the direct byte checks; it is not a new product acceptance report. No percentage of product completion is inferred from row counts.

## Three highest-impact implementable remaining increments

1. **Complete one exact-target native code/test/restore slice.** Extend the current read-only native adapter with a separately authorized, typed owned-test backend for the observed `start_stop_play`, `execute_luau`, `user_keyboard_input`/`user_mouse_input` and `screen_capture` tools. Bind native Studio ID to the freshly paired plugin lifetime without matching by display name/place ID 0; retain one writer/test owner, held-input cleanup and unknown-outcome receipts. First acceptance is one disposable proximity door: inspect, editor-aware change, real prompt input, authoritative server assertion, screenshot, stop and selective restore; include a dirty open-buffer conflict. File scopes: `packages/studio-adapter/src/{policy,session}.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/studio.ts`, `apps/daemon/src/native-routes.ts`, new `apps/daemon/src/studio-test-service.ts`, new `packages/storage/src/test-store.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/studio.ts`, narrow adapter/HTTP tests and a new disposable engine acceptance fixture. Keep current read-only callers read-only. Local protocol/lifecycle fixtures can be implemented without Studio; native acceptance waits for fresh human Reconnect and authorized engine execution. Installation and the empty-window inventory are not the remaining implementation themselves. Closes the critical M1–M3 journey, not every QA/device/multiplayer requirement.

2. **Make one same-chat code workflow execute a bounded inspect/plan/change/verify loop.** Connect existing native conversation identity, WorkStore/recipe gates, source baselines and action receipts to an explicit run controller. Show requested settings, turn/action IDs and known effects; enforce step/time/repair limits, safe pause/cancel and no repeated unknown `turn/start` or mutation. Revalidate the current target/source before commit and reject stale dependent partial changes. Use selected, hash-recorded skills only when explicitly eligible; approved-only stays empty until genuine behavior approval. File scopes: new `apps/daemon/src/task-controller.ts`, `apps/daemon/src/{workflow-service,workflow-host,workflow-native-model,codex-service}.ts`, `packages/storage/src/{work-store,workflow-store}.ts`, `packages/core/src/workflow-recipes.ts`, `packages/codex-client/src/{types,session}.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/{codex-chat,workflow-panel}.ts`, task-controller fixtures. First deliverable is a single code-change recipe with a deterministic source/compile check and an external engine-verification gate; do not label syntax compilation as type/runtime/gameplay verification. Offline protocol fixtures can prove scheduling, budget stops, recovery and dependency behavior. A later separately authorized native code task is required for completion; the consumed smoke approval cannot be reused. This closes an Arcane orchestration gap; richer Claude/media features remain capability-specific.

3. **Deliver owned static import and changed-only reimport.** Start with one asymmetric existing GLB/FBX asset. Implement a versioned import plan and persistent mapping of logical source objects/hashes to actual returned Studio object/container IDs and creator context. If a verified automated upload route is unavailable, provide an explicit supported Studio 3D Importer handoff followed by real result inspection; report the handoff as pending until reconciled. Require measured axes/scale/pivot/material checks, preserve gameplay children, and preview removed/changed objects before update. File scopes: `packages/asset-pipeline/src/types.ts`, new `packages/asset-pipeline/src/{import-plan,import-mapping}.ts`, new `packages/storage/src/asset-import-store.ts`, new `apps/daemon/src/asset-import-service.ts`, `apps/daemon/src/asset-routes.ts`, narrowly scoped `plugin/src/Operations.luau`/protocol extensions where needed, `apps/desktop/src/studio.ts`/asset review controls, import-plan/mapping fixtures and an asymmetric engine acceptance fixture. Implement ownership, idempotency, mapping and post-import verification locally first; do not invent an arbitrary mesh API or treat an uploaded ID as loadable. Actual importer/upload and engine checks need a supported route, creator permissions and separate authorization. First acceptance: import v1, change one mesh, reconcile v2 without a duplicate or lost user Script, then recover an interrupted update. Rigs/animations/reference craft stay explicitly open after this static slice.

## Provider/platform constraints versus Arcane gaps

**External constraints:** vendor eligibility/entitlement, richer native image/Design/browser/connector interfaces and reported effective effort/quota cannot be manufactured by Arcane. Claude subscription login is not authorization for an arbitrary embedded proxy; keep the genuine CLI handoff until a supported route is evidenced. Roblox's supported upload formats/creator permissions/moderation, input/client capabilities and Windows/macOS support constrain advertised behavior. Missing current permission or connection is a runtime precondition, not completion evidence. Current reconnect is human-owned.

**Arcane-fixable gaps:** exact cross-backend identity binding, allowed test adapters and cleanup, durable task dispatch, complete composer/history/editor/viewer controls, approval-safe skill evaluation infrastructure, static import mappings and reconciliation, general craft/rig/media workers, Git/project organization, redacted diagnostics and clean packaged acceptance. These can be implemented and fixture-tested before external runtime gates. Cloud/accounts/billing/teams and signing/update/support systems are also unimplemented product work, not provider limitations. They remain full-scope requirements even though the local alpha does not require them. Human gameplay/art review and real native integration cannot be replaced by fixture counts.
